children.name: Lead
children.text: Wärtsilä’s digital products run on two tracks: web portals for customers and employees, and machinery UI for crews and plant operators. Each track kept its own libraries and rules. CoreDS unites both under one guideline — shared usability principles, token naming and component specs — delivered as React components in Storybook.

Reviews 5 and 7 use the Design Quality Document as entry evidence; new projects enter via Conceptualize, renewing projects go from Correspond straight to In-Depth; failed reviews loop back.

children.name: Lead
children.text: One illustration grammar for every Brand Hub reader: real UI laid flat and tilted, with one orange accent per image. The illustrations are modular, so new chapters reuse parts instead of redrawing them.

children.name: b
children.text: Both axes sit at ±34°; the same CSS transform drives Figma and web illustrations.

children.name: b
children.text: One blue plus its opacities. Orange #FF7321 keeps its Foundations meaning — action and active state — and appears once per image.

children.name: b
children.text: Gap and radius fixed at 16, like a token, whether a module spans one cell or three.

children.name: b
children.text: Layers map to z-index: ground, plane, lifted focus card, upright cursor and hand.

caption.text: MODULAR DESIGN — the same KPI modules recombine from process page to plant dashboard, as defined in the Modular Dashboard pattern.

children.text: Example: the Advanced Vertical Linear Gauge of a local control unit. Auto Layout maps to Flexbox, every visual value is a token, states come from UX rules, and I built it in React + TypeScript with one story per state.
